questions.q: If $c=2 \cos \theta$, then the value of the determinant $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll}c & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & c & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & c\end{array}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
Given that $c=2 \cos \theta\therefore \Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll} c & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & c & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & c \end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 2 \cos \theta & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \cos \theta & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & 2 \cos \theta \end{array}\right|$
On expanding, we get $\begin{aligned} \Delta= & 2 \cos \theta\left[\left(4 \cos ^2 \theta-1\right)\right] \\ & \quad-1[(2 \cos \theta-6)]+0[(1-12 \cos \theta)] \\ = & 8 \cos ^3 \theta-2 \cos \theta-2 \cos \theta+6 \\ = & 8 \cos ^3 \theta-4 \cos \theta+6 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & a & a^2 \\ 1 & b & b^2 \\ 1 & c & c^2\end{array}\right|=k(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$, then $k$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & a & a^2 \\
1 & b & b^2 \\
1 & c & c^2
\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & a & a^2 \\
0 & b-a & b^2-a^2 \\
0 & c-a & c^2-a^2
\end{array}\right| \\
& \left(\text { using } R_2 \rightarrow R_2-R_1 \text { and } R_3 \rightarrow R_3-R_1\right) \\
& =(b-a)(c-a)\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & a & a^2 \\
0 & 1 & b+a \\
0 & 1 & c+a
\end{array}\right| \\
& =(b-a)(c-a)(c+a-b-a) \\
& \Rightarrow(b-a)(c-a)(c-b) \\
& =k(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)(given) \\
& \Rightarrow  k=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\Delta_1=\left|\begin{array}{lll}x & a & b \\ b & x & a \\ a & b & x\end{array}\right|$ and $\Delta_2=\left|\begin{array}{ll}x & b \\ a & x\end{array}\right|$ are the given determinants, then
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } \Delta_1=\left|\begin{array}{lll}x & a & b \\ b & x & a \\ a & b & x\end{array}\right|, \Delta_2=\left|\begin{array}{ll}x & b \\ a & x\end{array}\right| \\ & \begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{d}{d x}\left(\Delta_1\right) \\ &=\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & 0 & 0 \\ b & x & a \\ a & b & x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{lll}x & a & b \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ a & b & x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{lll}x & a & b \\ b & x & a \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right| \\ & \quad=\left|\begin{array}{ll}x & a \\ b & x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ll}x & b \\ a & x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ll}x & a \\ b & x\end{array}\right|=3 \Delta_2 \\ & \therefore \frac{d}{d x}\left(\Delta_1\right)=3 \Delta_2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The value of ' $a$ ' for which the system of equations
$a x+y+z=0, x+a y+z=0, x+y+z=0$
possesses non-zero solutions are given by
questions.solution:
Given, system of equations are
$\begin{aligned} & a x+y+z=0, x+a y+z=0 \\ & \text { and } x+y+z=0 \text { possesses non-zero solution. }\end{aligned}\therefore \quad\left|\begin{array}{lll}a & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & a & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right|=0\begin{array}{rr}\Rightarrow & a(a-1)-1(1-1)+1(1-a)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & a^2-a+0+1-a=0 \\ \Rightarrow & a^2-2 a+1=0 \\ \Rightarrow & (a-1)^2=0 \\ \Rightarrow & a=1\end{array}$

questions.q: If $a, b$ and $c$ are negative and different real numbers, then $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{array}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{array}\right|$
Applying, $C_1 \rightarrow C_1+C_2+C_3$ and taking common from $C_1\begin{aligned} \Delta & =(a+b+c)\left|\begin{array}{lll} 1 & b & c \\ 1 & c & a \\ 1 & a & b \end{array}\right| \\ & =-(a+b+c)\left[a^2+b^2+c^2-a b-b c-c a\right] \\ & =-\frac{(a+b+c)}{2}\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right] \\ & \gt0 \text { as } a, b, c \lt 0 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\quad D_k=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a & 2^k & 2^{16}-1 \\ b & 3\left(4^k\right) & 2\left(4^{16}-1\right) \\ c & 7\left(8^k\right) & 4\left(8^{16}-1\right)\end{array}\right|$, then the value of $\sum_{k=1}^{16} D_k$ is
questions.solution:
We have,
$\sum_{k=1}^{16} D_k=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a & \left(\sum_{k=1}^{16} 2^k\right) & 2^{16}-1 \\ b & 3\left(\sum_{k=1}^{16} 4^4\right) & 2\left(4^{16}-1\right) \\ C & 7\left(\sum_{k=1}^{16} 8^k\right) & 4\left(8^{16}-1\right)\end{array}\right|\Rightarrow \quad \sum_{k=1}^{16} D_k=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a & 2\left(\frac{2^{16}-1}{2-1}\right) & 2^{16}-1 \\ b & 3 \times 4\left(\frac{4^{16}-1}{4-1}\right) & 2\left(4^{16}-1\right) \\ c & 7 \times 8\left(\frac{8^{16}-1}{8-1}\right) & 4\left(8^{16}-1\right)\end{array}\right|\Rightarrow \quad \sum_{k=1}^{16} D_k=\left|\begin{array}{lll}a & 2\left(2^{16}-1\right) & \left(2^{16}-1\right) \\ b & 4\left(4^{16}-1\right) & 2\left(4^{16}-1\right) \\ c & 8\left(8^{16}-1\right) & 4\left(8^{16}-1\right)\end{array}\right|\Rightarrow \quad \sum_{k=1}^{16} D_k=2\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a & \left(2^{16}-1\right) & \left(2^{16}-1\right) \\ b & 2\left(4^{16}-1\right) & 2\left(4^{16}-1\right) \\ c & 4\left(8^{16}-1\right) & 4\left(8^{16}-1\right)\end{array}\right|$
[taking 2 common from $C_2$ ]
$\Rightarrow \quad \sum_{k=1}^{16} D_k=2 \times 0=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\lambda$ and $\mu$ for which the system of equations $x+y+z=6, x+2 y+3 z=10$ and $x+2 y+\lambda z=\mu$ have no solution, are
questions.solution:
Given system of equation is $\begin{aligned} x+y+z & =6 \\ x+2 y+3 z & =10 \\ x+2 y+\lambda z & =\mu \end{aligned}$
If given system of equation has no solution, then $D=0$ and atleast one of the determinants $D_1, D_2, D_3 \neq 0\begin{aligned} & \text { Here } \\ & \begin{aligned} & D=0 \\ &\left|\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & \lambda \end{array}\right|=0 \end{aligned} \\ & \Rightarrow 1(2 \lambda-6)-1(\lambda-3)+1(2-2)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \lambda-6-\lambda+3+0=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \lambda-3=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \lambda=3 \end{aligned}$
Also, $D_1=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & 2 & 3 \\ \mu & 2 & 3\end{array}\right| \neq 0\begin{array}{rlrl} \Rightarrow & 6(6-6)-1(30-3 \mu)+1(20-2 \mu) & \neq 0 \\ \Rightarrow & 0-30+3 \mu+20-2 \mu \neq 0 \\ \Rightarrow & \mu-10 \neq 0 \\ \Rightarrow & \mu \neq 10 \end{array}$

questions.q: Coefficient of $x$ in $f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x & (1+\sin x)^3 & \cos x \\ 1 & \log (1+x) & 2 \\ x^2 & (1+x)^2 & 0\end{array}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
Coefficient $x$ in $f(x)$ is equal to coefficient of $x$ in
$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x & \left(1+x-\frac{x^3}{3!} \ldots\right)^3 & 1-\frac{x^2}{2!} \\ 1 & x-\frac{x^2}{2} & 2 \\ x^2 & 1+x^2 & 0\end{array}\right|=$ coefficient of $x$ in $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & x & 2 \\ x^2 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right|\begin{aligned} & =\text { Coefficient of } x \text { in }\left[x(0-2)-1\left(0-2 x^2\right)\right. \\ & \left.+1\left(1-x^3\right)\right]\end{aligned}=-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\alpha_1, \alpha_2$ and $\beta_1, \beta_2$ be the roots of $a x^2+b x+c=0 \quad$ and $\quad p x^2+q x+r=0$ respectively. If the system of equations $\alpha_1 y+\alpha_2 z=0$ and $\beta_1 y+\beta_2 z=0$ has $a$ non-trivial solution, then
questions.solution:
Given system has non-trivial solution then
$\left|\begin{array}{ll}\alpha_1 & \alpha_2 \\ \beta_1 & \beta_2\end{array}\right|=0\Rightarrow \quad \alpha_1 \beta_2=\alpha_2 \beta_1\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \frac{\alpha_1}{\beta_1}=\frac{\alpha_2}{\beta_2}=\frac{\alpha_1+\alpha_2}{\beta_1+\beta_2}=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_1 \alpha_2}{\beta_1 \beta_2}} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{-b / a}{-q / p}=\sqrt{\frac{c / a}{r / p}} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{b p}{a q}=\sqrt{\frac{c p}{a r}} \\ \Rightarrow & b^2 p^2 a r=a^2 q^2 c p \\ \Rightarrow & b^2 p r=q^2 a c\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\omega=-\frac{1}{2}+i \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, then value of the determinant $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1-\omega^2 & \omega^2 \\ 1 & \omega^2 & \omega\end{array}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
Applying $\quad R_2 \rightarrow R_2-R_1 ; \quad R_3 \rightarrow R_3-R_1$, the given determinant becomes
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 1 & 1 \\
0 & -2-\omega^2 & \omega^2-1 \\
0 & \omega^2-1 & \omega-1
\end{array}\right| \\
& =1\left[(\omega-1)\left(-2-\omega^2\right)-\left\{\left(\omega^2-1\right)\left(\omega^2-1\right)\right\}\right] -1(0)+1(0) \\
& =\left(-2-\omega^2\right)(\omega-1)-\left(\omega^2-1\right)^2 \\
& =-2 \omega+2-\omega^3+\omega^2-\left(\omega^4+1-2 \omega^2\right) \\
& =-2 \omega+1+\omega^2-\left(\omega+1-2 \omega^2\right) \\
& =3 \omega^2-3 \omega \\
& =3 \omega(\omega-1)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Let $\lambda$ and $\alpha$ be real
$\begin{array}{r}
\lambda x+\sin \alpha \cdot y+\cos \alpha \cdot z=0 \\
x+\cos \alpha \cdot y+\sin \alpha \cdot z=0 \\
-x+\sin \alpha \cdot y-\cos \alpha \cdot z=0
\end{array}$
has a non-trivial solution. If $\lambda=1$, then all the values of $\alpha$ is equals
questions.solution:
The given system has a non-trivial solution, if $\left|\begin{array}{rrr} \lambda & \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \\ 1 & \cos \alpha & \sin \alpha \\ -1 & \sin \alpha & -\cos \alpha \end{array}\right|=0$
By expanding the determinant along ( $C_1$ ), we get $\begin{gathered} \lambda\left(-\cos ^2 \alpha-\sin ^2 \alpha\right)-1(-\sin \alpha \cos \alpha \\ -\sin \alpha \cos \alpha) \\ -1\left(\sin ^2 \alpha-\cos ^2 \alpha\right)=0 \\ \lambda=\sin 2 \alpha+\cos 2 \alpha \end{gathered}$ For $\quad \lambda=1, \sin 2 \alpha+\cos 2 \alpha=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin 2 \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos 2 \alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow \quad \cos \left(2 \alpha-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\cos \left(2 n \pi \pm \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\Rightarrow 2 \alpha=2 n \pi \pm \frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{4}, n$ being an integer. $\Rightarrow \quad \alpha=n \pi+\frac{\pi}{4}, n \pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A+B+C=\pi$, then $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin (A+B+C) & \sin B & \cos C \\ -\sin B & 0 & \tan A \\ \cos ^{\prime}(A+B) & -\tan A & 0\end{array}\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
In a triangle $A B C$,
$A+B+C=\pi,\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sin (A+B+C)=0, \cos (A+B)=-\cos C \\ & \therefore\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin (A+B+C) & \sin B & \cos C \\ -\sin B & 0 & \tan A \\ \cos (A+B) & -\tan A & 0\end{array}\right| \\ & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & \sin B & \cos C \\ -\sin B & 0 & \tan A \\ -\cos C & -\tan A & 0\end{array}\right| \\ & =0\end{aligned}\left(\begin{array}{rl}\because & \text { It is the determinant of a skew } \\ \text { symmetric matrix of odd order. }\end{array}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x+y+2 z & x & y \\ z & y+z+2 x & y \\ z & x & z+x+2 y\end{array}\right|=k(x+y+z)^3$, then the value of $k$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \Delta & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} x+y+2 z & x & y \\ z & y+z+2 x & y \\ z & x & z+x+2 y \end{array}\right| \\ & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 2(x+y+z) & x & y \\ 2(x+y+z) & y+z+2 x & y \\ 2(x+y+z) & x & z+x+2 y \end{array}\right| \end{aligned}$ (using $C_1 \rightarrow C_1+C_2+C_3$ ) Take out $2(x+y+z)$ common from $C_1$, we get $\begin{aligned} & \Delta=2(x+y+z)\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & x & y \\ 1 & y+z+2 x & y \\ 1 & x & z+x+2 y \end{array}\right| \\ & =2(x+y+z)\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & x & y \\ 0 & y+z+x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & z+x+y \end{array}\right| \end{aligned}$ (using $R_2 \rightarrow R_2-R_1, R_3 \rightarrow R_3-R_1$ ) Take out $(x+y+z)$ common from $R_2$ and $R_3$, we get $\begin{aligned} \Delta=2(x+y+z)(x+y+z)(x+y & +z) \\ & \times\left|\begin{array}{lll} 1 & x & y \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right| \end{aligned}$
Expanding along $R_3$, we get $\begin{aligned} \Delta & =2(x+y+z)^3[(1)(1-0)] \\ & =2(x+y+z)^3=k(x+y+z)^3 \text { (given) } \\ \therefore \quad k & =2 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of the determinant $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\left(a^x+a^{-x}\right)^2 & \left(a^x-a^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ \left(b^x+b^{-x}\right)^2 & \left(b^x-b^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ \left(c^x+c^{-x}\right)^2 & \left(c^x-c^{-x}\right)^2 & 1\end{array}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
Given determinant is $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \left(a^x+a^{-x}\right)^2 & \left(a^x-a^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ \left(b^x+b^{-x}\right)^2 & \left(b^x-b^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ \left(c^x+c^{-x}\right)^2 & \left(c^x-c^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \end{array}\right|$
Applying $C_1 \rightarrow C_1-C_2$, we get $\begin{aligned} \Delta & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 4 & \left(a^x-a^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ 4 & \left(b^x-b^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ 4 & \left(c^x-c^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \end{array}\right|=4\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 1 & \left(a^x-a^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ 1 & \left(b^x-b^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \\ 1 & \left(c^x-c^{-x}\right)^2 & 1 \end{array}\right| \\ & =0 \quad(\because \text { two columns are identical) } \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\quad \Delta_r=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & n & n \\ 2 r & n^2+n+1 & n^2+n \\ 2 r-1 & n^2 & n^2+n+1\end{array}\right| \quad$ and $\sum_{r=1}^n \Delta_r=56$, then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Putting $r=1,2,3, \ldots, n$ and using the formula $\begin{aligned} & \Sigma 1=n \\ & \text { and } \quad \Sigma r=\frac{n(n+1)}{2} \\ & \Sigma(2 r-1)=1+3+5+\ldots=n^2 \\ & \therefore \sum_{r=1}^n \Delta_r=\left|\begin{array}{cc} n & n \\ n(n+1) & n^2+n+1 \\ n^2 & n^2 \end{array} c \begin{array}{l} n^2+n \\ n^2+n+1 \end{array}\right|=56 \end{aligned}$
Applying $C_1 \rightarrow C_1-C_3, C_2 \rightarrow C_2-C_3$, we get $\begin{aligned} &\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 0 & n \\ 0 & 1 & n^2+n \\ -n-1 & -n-1 & n^2+n+1 \end{array}\right|=56 \\ & \Rightarrow \\ & \Rightarrow n(n+1)=56 \\ & \Rightarrow \\ & n^2+n-56=0 \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & (n+8)(n-7) & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & n & =7,(n \neq-8)\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The values of $\lambda$ such that $(x, y, z) \neq(0,0,0)$ and
$(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) x+(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) y+(-4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}) z=\lambda(\hat{\mathbf{i}} x+\hat{\mathbf{j}} y+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \boldsymbol{z})$ are
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned} &(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) x+(3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) y \\ &+(-4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+5 \hat{\mathbf{j}}) z=\lambda(\hat{\mathbf{i}} x+\hat{\mathbf{j}} y+\hat{\mathbf{k}} z)\end{aligned}$
On equating the coefficients of $\hat{\mathbf{i}}, \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ both sides, we have
$\begin{aligned} & x+3 y-4 z=\lambda x \\ & x-3 y+5 z=\lambda y\end{aligned}$
and $\quad 3 x+y+0=\lambda z$
Above three equations can be rewritten as
$\begin{array}{r}(1-\lambda) x+3 y-4 z=0 \\ x-(3+\lambda) y+5 z=0 \\ 3 x+y-\lambda z=0\end{array}
This is homogeneous system of equations in three variables $x, y$ and $z$.
It is consistent and have non-zero solution. i.e. $(x, y, z) \neq(0,0,0)$, if determinant of coefficient matrix is zero.
$\Rightarrow \quad\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1-\therefore & 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -(3+\lambda) & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & -\lambda\end{array}\right|=0$
On expanding along first row, we have
$\begin{aligned}(1-\lambda)[\lambda(3+\lambda)-5]-3(-\lambda-15) & \\ & -4(1+9+3 \lambda)=0\end{aligned}\begin{array}{cc}\Rightarrow & (1-\lambda)\left(\lambda^2+3 \lambda-5\right)+3 \lambda+45-40-12 \lambda=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda^2+3 \lambda-5-\lambda^3-3 \lambda^2+5 \lambda-9 \lambda+5=0 \\ \Rightarrow & -\lambda^3-2 \lambda^2-\lambda=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda\left(\lambda^2+2 \lambda+1\right)=0\end{array}
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \lambda(\lambda+1)^2 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda & =0,-1\end{aligned}$
